claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The splashdown marked the end of a 10-day mission.
The mission had a crew of four.
The crew of four was in good health.
The Artemis II Orion capsule was successfully retrieved by Navy teams.
The Artemis II Orion capsule hit the water at approximately 20 mph.
Five orange airbags activated to flip the Artemis II Orion capsule upright.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed, deep-space journey of the Artemis program.
The Artemis II mission is designed to test equipment for future lunar surface landings.
The Artemis II crew is set to be extracted from the Artemis II Orion capsule by Amentum recovery teams.
The Artemis II crew is set to return to the Navy vessel
